summary: Researched the evening before (Sat 21 Nov); lineups are not out, so this is a draft until the morning check and the final check. Sunday has Serie A, La Liga, Ligue 1 and Premier League football, seven NFL games and one NHL game; basketball is not researched (the owner's permanent rule). Medium: Juventus, Barcelona, Brighton (at Hull), Inter (at Atalanta), Marseille, and in the NFL the Bears, Cowboys, Lions, Jaguars and Steelers, plus the Lightning in the NHL. Low: Paris FC (ClubElo and the Sports Mole model about 15 points under the market), Milan (price down 3.1% in 24h with no news) and the Chargers (a 1-8 favourite at about 60%). Excluded as derbies or fierce rivalries on a conservative reading: Getafe v Atlético (Madrid-area derby) and Broncos v Raiders (historic AFC West rivalry). Views that contradicted a game's own main risk were dropped (Barcelona over 2.5, Juventus over 1.5, Inter over 2.5 and both teams to score). Morning check (Sun 22 Nov): no overnight news hurts Brighton, Inter or the Steelers. Brighton firmed (+3.1% since first listing, explained by easing team news and matched by DraftKings), Inter are unchanged, the Steelers eased 1.5% after Herbig was ruled out. Lineups and NFL inactives are not out, so this is still a draft until the final check.

Saints last 5: L 20-17 at CAR (15 Nov), W 23-22 CLE (8 Nov), L 10-16 PIT, W 34-27 NYG, L 13-23 MIN; they have 3 wins in 9 games and allowed 45 to ATL. Bears 7-2 vs Saints 3-6.

Windy and possibly wet conditions help the underdog slightly by shortening the game. Note that ESPN lists the Bears as the home side and Polymarket names the Saints first, so the candidate keys are home=Saints, away=Bears.

games.reason: The Bears are 7-2 at home against a 3-6 Saints side missing three offensive linemen. The DraftKings de-vigged price (0.829) and ESPN's predictor (78.6%) both support the Polymarket 0.845, so the price is slightly rich but within range. The confidence is medium because the starting QBs and Friday final statuses are not confirmed, the spread of -11.5 leaves room for a late game, and the Bears have a Thanksgiving game on Thursday.
games.main_risk: Close game decided late: Caleb Williams turnovers (5 INT) and wind of 21 mph with possible rain on a 11.5-point spread keep the score tight, and a mid-week look-ahead to Detroit on Thanksgiving. Backup-QB risk is low on the evidence (neither QB on the injury list) but inactives are not out yet.

games.reason: HARD rule "derby or fierce rivalry", conservative reading (as for Getafe v Atlético the same day): Broncos-Raiders is a historic AFC West rivalry with its own Wikipedia article (73-58-2 series, a 2017 sideline brawl, the 1995 Shanahan dispute, the most Monday Night Football meetings in NFL history). The research otherwise found Denver a clear favourite (7-2, 4-0 at home, rested after a bye; DraftKings about 0.824 de-vigged, ESPN FPI about 86%) against a 4-6 Raiders side with a rookie QB.
games.main_risk: A close, low-scoring division game (total 40.5) decided late or by turnovers: Nix has 4 interceptions, a rookie Mendoza can still hit a big play against Denver, and rivalry games are tighter than the ratings suggest. A late scratch to Nix is the other risk (not on the injury report, inactives not yet out). Rivalry classification is a judgement call: it counts as a notable divisional rivalry, not a derby.

games.reason: A strong home favourite, top of the table, with a real title incentive against a mid-table side that has nothing at stake. DraftKings (79.4% de-vigged) agrees with Polymarket (81.4%) within 2 points, and the 24h price move is zero. No hard exclusion applies: it is not a derby, no coach change, and a normal venue. Confidence is medium rather than high because lineups are unconfirmed, the centre-back news is conflicting (Cubarsi), and no Elo rating could be read.
games.main_risk: A draw or an away win, most likely through a low-scoring game where Barcelona create chances but Villarreal sit deep, or through defensive weakness if Cubarsi is out. Barcelona already have a league loss and two recent defeats (Real Madrid, PSG) in the form string. A one-goal win would sink the -1.5 handicap and the Over 2.5 goals leg, so I give no view on the handicaps or Barcelona team-goals legs.

Set to low when merged: the two bookmaker-free models sit about 15 points under the market, a doubt the 5-point limit on p cannot reflect, and Paris FC failed to score in both recent meetings.
